Grey Mode recovery is a complete closed negative-feedback regulator in code: its sensor (compute_psi_r), comparator (reentry_test, against an adaptive threshold) and actuator (recovery_cycle) sit in one class, and the actuator's output is the sensor's next input.

CASCADE closes a feedback loop across calls through shared state: _execute_cascade writes each block's regime, and contradicts() reads it when the next block arrives. Reading this as Ashby's double-loop ultrastability is an interpretation, not a measurement.

The AURA constitutional check, the TRI-AXIAL check and the MICROORCIM daily tracker are open loops in code: each senses and compares, and none acts. The single-pass sovereign pipeline entry point (`SovereignPipeline.run`, `L-PIPELINE`) is feedforward (CASCADE to TRIAD to AURA to stateless MICROORCIM drift); nothing its last stage measures returns to its first, closing only through a person or host model that reads the verdict. The opt-in bounded regulator entry point (`SovereignPipeline.regulate`, `L-PIPELINE-REGULATOR`, SCAFFOLD) closes in code only when supplied an explicit caller correction policy, regulating the implemented coherence and text-score proxy across a finite evaluation budget with visible refusal on budget exhaustion or policy failure (synthetic/internal proxy evidence only; does not establish factual truth or real-world effects).

An invariant-gated generator (propose candidate actions, admit only those that pass a constraint check) can meet disturbances no rule anticipated, as Ashby's law of requisite variety requires, under two conditions only: the generator has the variety the disturbances demand, and the gate's sensor reads the essential variable rather than a proxy. Without the first it refuses, a visible failure; without the second it admits wrong actions with confidence, a silent failure. Shown in a synthetic toy world; not measured on any language model.
